iturn0image0turn0image1turn0image2turn0image7May 2025 offers several notable celestial events for skywatchers in Glendale, Arizona, and beyond. Here's a guide to the key astronomical highlights:

---

### 🌠 Eta Aquariid Meteor Shower (Peak: May 5–6)

The Eta Aquariids, originating from Halley's Comet, peaked on the night of May 5 into the early hours of May 6. While the peak has passed, the meteor shower remains active until May 21. Observers can still catch meteors in the pre-dawn hours, especially under dark skies away from city lights. citeturn0search7

---

### 🌕 Flower Full Moon (May 12)

The Full Moon on May 12, known as the "Flower Moon," was the last Micromoon of 2025, appearing slightly smaller due to its position at the farthest point in its orbit from Earth. The Moon will continue to appear nearly full for a couple of nights following the peak. citeturn0search15

---

### 🌌 Planetary Alignment: Saturn, Moon, and Venus (May 22–24)

From May 22 to May 24, early risers can witness a striking alignment of Saturn, the crescent Moon, and Venus in the eastern pre-dawn sky. On May 22, the Moon will be near Saturn; on May 23, it will sit close to Venus, with "Earthshine" potentially visible on the Moon's dark side. By May 24, the Moon will be a thin crescent approaching its new phase. citeturn0news19

---

### 🌑 New Moon (May 27)

The New Moon on May 27 will provide optimal dark-sky conditions for stargazing, as the absence of moonlight enhances visibility of faint celestial objects. citeturn0search15

---

### 🌌 Milky Way Visibility (Late May)

Late May offers excellent opportunities to observe the Milky Way, especially between midnight and 5 a.m. With the New Moon on May 27 and clear spring skies, the galaxy's star-filled band will be prominent. For the best experience, find a location with minimal light pollution and look southward. citeturn0news21

---

For more detailed information on these and other astronomical events, you can refer to resources like the [Sea and Sky Astronomy Calendar](https://www.seasky.org/astronomy/astronomy-calendar-2025.html) or [Star Walk's Astronomy Calendar](https://starwalk.space/en/news/astronomy-calendar-2025).

Happy stargazing!
